chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The blind and the seated cripple are not valid for emancipation, and the one with a hand defect and the lame are valid.'

key_terms.الْأَشَلُّ: The one with a defect in the hand/arm

ai.seo_question: Which physical disabilities invalidate the emancipation of a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the juristic criteria for the validity of manumitting a slave (ittaq) by distinguishing between severe physical impairments that invalidate the act and minor ones that do. Specifically, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while blindness and immobility (al-muq'ad) render emancipation invalid, defects like a hand impairment (al-ashal) or lameness (al-a'raj) do not, reflecting the Shia scholarly focus on the functional capacity of the slave in legal transactions.
